name: Home Economics
strapline: Skills for food, wellbeing and everyday life.
intro: Explore food choices, preparation, sustainability and product development. Home Economics is an umbrella: Practical Cookery and Health and Food Technology are different qualifications. Suggested BGE projects need departmental review. Follow teacher instructions, allergy arrangements and school food-safety procedures for all practical work; independent hub tasks use menus, labels and planning.

bge.title: Food and our choices
bge.question: What influences what we eat?
bge.task: Compare two fictional lunch options using cost, variety and suitability, without labelling a person’s food choices.
bge.extend: Identify information needed before planning for a group with allergies.

bge.title: Kitchen organisation
bge.question: Why does planning matter?
bge.task: Reorder a supplied preparation plan and explain two safety-critical stages.
bge.extend: Explain why cleaning and separating raw and ready-to-eat foods are different controls.

bge.title: Food waste detectives
bge.question: How can resources go further?
bge.task: Use a fictional household shopping list to propose three waste-reduction changes.
bge.extend: Explain why a use-by date should not be treated like a best-before date.

bge.title: Develop a product
bge.question: How do we know a food meets a brief?
bge.task: Design a paper-based snack concept for a stated brief, with ingredients and evaluation criteria.
bge.extend: Explain how coded samples could reduce bias in a teacher-organised sensory test.

senior.title: Practical Cookery
senior.explain: Develop safe practical preparation and organisation. National 4 includes added-value practical work.
senior.assessment: Internal assessment, with added value at National 4; pass/fail.

senior.title: National 5 Practical Cookery
senior.explain: A practical qualification focused on preparation, cooking and presentation. There is no Higher Practical Cookery.
senior.assessment: For session 2026–27 the assignment has been removed. Use the current specification for the question paper and practical activity requirements.

senior.title: Health and Food Technology
senior.explain: A separate course connecting nutrition, consumer issues and food product development. National 4 includes added value.
senior.assessment: National 4 is internally assessed; National 5 uses a question paper and assignment under current conditions.

source.title: Qualifications Scotland — Health and Food Technology

senior.title: Higher Health and Food Technology
senior.explain: Analyse food needs, functional properties, product development and contemporary issues in greater depth. This is a different route from Practical Cookery.
senior.assessment: Question paper and assignment; discuss entry and availability with the department.

source.title: Qualifications Scotland — Higher Health and Food Technology

skills.title: Read a label
skills.explain: Compare like-for-like quantities and identify the relevant information.
skills.try: Compare sugar per 100 g and per portion for two fictional products.
skills.check: Explain how portion size can change the apparent comparison.

skills.title: Plan a workflow
skills.explain: Organise tasks so timing, hygiene and resources work together.
skills.try: Annotate a teacher-provided plan with storage and cleaning checkpoints.
skills.check: Show which tasks can overlap safely and which require separation.

skills.title: Evaluate a food product
skills.explain: Use criteria linked to a brief rather than personal preference alone.
skills.try: Write three criteria for a convenient school snack concept.
skills.check: Each criterion should be specific enough to evaluate.

skills.title: Analyse evidence
skills.explain: Food claims need reliable evidence and appropriate context.
skills.try: Identify the source and audience of a food advertisement.
skills.check: Distinguish a marketing claim from evidence and avoid personalised health conclusions.

practice.question: Product A has 12 g sugar per 100 g and a 25 g portion. How much sugar is in that portion?
practice.hint: Find one quarter of the per-100 g figure.
practice.answer: 12 × 25/100 = 3 g. Use the same basis when comparing products; a smaller printed portion can make values look lower.
practice.extend: Compare with a product containing 10 g per 100 g in a 40 g portion.

practice.question: Why is using the same unwashed board for raw chicken and ready-to-eat salad unsafe?
practice.hint: The salad has no later cooking step.
practice.answer: Microorganisms may transfer from raw poultry to food that will be eaten without further cooking. Follow school procedures for separate equipment, cleaning and hand hygiene.
practice.extend: Identify how a workflow plan could prevent that transfer.

practice.question: A developer asks five friends whether a new food is “the best ever”. Why is this weak evaluation?
practice.answer: The sample is small and unrepresentative, and the leading question encourages praise. Use neutral questions and criteria linked to the brief; teacher-organised coded comparisons can reduce bias.

resources.title: Food Standards Scotland
resources.task: Find food-safety guidance and explain one rule using its purpose, not just its wording.

resources.title: Food a fact of life cooking skills
resources.task: Review a teacher-selected technique resource. Practical use remains supervised and school-directed.

resources.title: Food a fact of life nutritional analysis
resources.task: Analyse a supplied recipe as a learning exercise; do not use it for personalised dietary advice.

resources.title: Zero Waste Scotland
resources.task: Investigate food-waste prevention and identify a feasible planning change.

resources.title: Official assessment information
resources.task: Check current assessment changes before using an older Practical Cookery resource.

ipad.title: Workflow designer
steps: Use a teacher-provided recipe on screen.
Create an ordered timeline with safety checkpoints.
Explain two sequencing decisions in audio and captions.
ipad.evidence: A clear preparation plan ready for teacher feedback.

ipad.title: Label comparison
steps: Create a comparison table on a consistent basis.
Write a cautious conclusion explaining portion size.

ipad.title: Product development journal
steps: Sketch a concept against a stated brief.
Add teacher-approved feedback from a class activity.
Show a revised version and justify one change.
ipad.evidence: A record of design decisions, not live assignment content.

careers.nextStep: Compare college food science and university food technology routes.

careers.nextStep: Investigate relevant degree and professional training requirements.

careers.nextStep: Explore college hospitality courses and employer training routes.

parentTip: Talk through a shopping list, label or meal plan. Keep discussion respectful of culture, budget and individual needs; school practicals follow agreed allergy and safety procedures.
